rules.why: A token of the build's own informers that a poll sends back; each build has its own and no screen shows it.
When this build filled its own minute of the answer; the two builds fill theirs moments apart.
OpenCost's window runs up to the moment a build filled its minute of the answer. number-check-cost.spec.ts holds these numbers to OpenCost.
The cluster's metrics at the moment each build asked, kept for its own moments. number-check-monitoring.spec.ts holds them to the Prometheus.
These lists come in Go map order, another order per computation. Stays while the compared build has them unsorted.
The graph's nodes come in Go map order per computation, kept while cached. Stays while the compared build has them unsorted.
Objects created in one second came in whichever list answered first. Stays while the compared build has no second key.
The GPUs come in Go map order per computation. Stays while the compared build has them unsorted.
This route did not exist in v0.7.5 (404): the Pods list paged by the server.
These routes did not exist in v0.7.5 (404): Cluster View's node map and one node's pods.
A live update was the raw object and is now the list row, so the row is named without its kind and the raw object's cells go.
A live update is now the same row as the list (internal/endpointslice), which every cell of the row under its new name is.
The list row now carries the slice's endpoints, labels and annotations.
A Service's slices are the same row as the EndpointSlice list.
The summary says how many of the counted events are listed.
The summary adds the events of the type asked; namespace and cluster rollouts now include StatefulSet and DaemonSet revisions.
Event times and counts as kubectl's printEvent reads them (eventTime and series for events.k8s.io writers, 1 for one seen once).
The event's object carries its apiVersion so the page opens the right group's custom resource.
Drawers' events as kubectl prints them; first_time and last_time, which no screen read, are now first_timestamp and last_timestamp, which the Events table reads.
Past reviews page: the server honours limit=25 (v0.7.5 ignored it and sent 100) and says the total in X-Kubeast-Total; the cells are rows 26 to 100.
The access review's dormant lock settings, full admins and total requests.
The admin list of access requests pages on the server and says its total.
Audit log pages keep the first read (as_of) and say the CSV's limit.
AI usage reads chat and alert investigations with totals over every group; each row names its source and the investigator has a row of its own.
The new permission resource.alert.investigate.
Skip reasons with their catalog key, the severities the alerts carry, and the inbox ordered by status, last received, then id.
The inbox says who asked for an investigation and when it was received.
The investigations list answers the skip reason's catalog key and arguments.
alert_investigations.requested_by tells a person's request from the webhook's.
Each model says what it is used for.
The screen now asks with_unlisted=1, which answers {items, forbidden_kinds, failed_kinds}; the rows are the same rows under items (the old build ignores the parameter and sends the array).
The per-CRD list carries each row's printer cells from the API server's Table.
Custom resource describe is the list's row (customResourceRows) with its metadata.
Advanced Search reads in pages up to the limit and says whether the list was cut.
Each object's kubectl STATUS, the Status column of the API server's Table.
The live update now carries what the list row has (ws deploymentToInfo).
A ReplicaSet with none available is Unavailable, not Degraded: none available is now checked first.
A box says what its list says (a pod's Status, a workload's summary status) and carries its health; a Deployment past its deadline reads Failed with #603.
A Role or ClusterRole a binding names has no status: the graph lists none.
A check's summary adds its findings by their own severity.
A pod finding's owner carries its apiVersion so its link opens the right group.
The served versions, kubectl's VERSIONS column, next to the storage version.
Mount options of a class with none are an empty list instead of null (internal/storageclass).
Access modes are the volume's once the claim is bound, empty before, as kubectl's printPersistentVolumeClaim; what the claim asks for is requested_access_modes.
The Namespace drawer's Resource Summary comes from describe (phases and sums); summed_pods came with #522.
nvidia.com/gpu and each nvidia.com/mig-* are added up, a GPU in use counts as kubectl describe node does, and the driver version keeps its revision.
GPUs per company: device_plugins replaces device_plugin_status, which the new screens no longer read.
The pods holding a GPU through a DRA claim are named.
DCGM labels in either spelling: hostname as well as Hostname, pod and namespace where the scrape kept them.
The features say when a grant limited to namespaces is refused the cluster's Prometheus.
Usage as kubectl top prints it: CPU rounded up, percents of the allocatable cut down. number-check-monitoring.spec.ts holds these numbers.
The VPA's target carries its apiVersion for the drawer link.
VPA's minReplicas, evictAfterOOMSeconds and startupBoost fields.
One row for the list and the live updates (internal/gatewayrow): the fields the pages read, which v0.7.5's list row left out or named otherwise.
A live update was the raw object and is now the list row, so the row is named without its kind and the raw object's cells go.
A live update is now the same row as the list (internal/gatewayrow), which every cell of the row under its new name is.
These three had no live updates in v0.7.5 (unsupported resource); on a cluster without the kind the answer is now the API server's own.
These four kinds had no live updates in v0.7.5 (unsupported resource); they are watched and send the list's row (internal/drarow).
One row for a DeviceClass (internal/drarow): cluster-scoped, so no namespace; labels never null; a count of 0 is sent.
One row for a claim and its template (internal/drarow): the claim's State as kubectl's resourceClaimState; labels never null.
A slice's Node, Driver and Pool are spec.nodeName, spec.driver and spec.pool.name; the old top-level fields were always empty.
Describe computes the drawer's claims using the class.
Describe computes the claim's State and the pods using it.
Describe computes the claims made from the template.
IngressClass describe reads the object's events and metadata.
Endpoints describe reads the object's events and uid.
The admission policies list the events about them.
ClusterRole rules are as the API has them: a rule with no names leaves the key out instead of sending null.
CRD describe returns its events.
A grant limited to namespaces lists its namespaces as the user instead of being refused the whole cluster; the rows are that namespace's only.
A grant limited to namespaces reads a node's pods in its namespaces instead of being refused.
Events are read in the order their times say since kubectl's printEvent rules; rows of one second have no order of their own.
The dev image is built WITH_CLAUDE_CODE and the compared release tag is the one without it, not a difference in the code.
